entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Joseph of Freising, also known as Joseph of Verona, was Bishop of Freising from 747 or 748 until his death on January 17, 764. He played a crucial role in the Frankish Empire's administrative and ecclesiastical governance, overseeing the conversion of the Saxons to Christianity and the establishment of the Diocese of Freising. This tenure marked a pivotal moment in the history of the Catholic Church, as Freising became a major center for the transmission of theological knowledge and liturgical practices.

    Joseph of Freising's significance extends beyond his ecclesiastical duties, as he was also a patron of the arts and architecture. He commissioned numerous buildings and monuments throughout his diocese, including the Freising Cathedral, which still stands today as a testament to his enduring legacy.

    The impact of Joseph of Freising's life and work can be seen in the many institutions and traditions he helped to establish. The Diocese of Freising continues to thrive, and its influence can be felt throughout the region. His legacy serves as a reminder of the enduring power of faith and the importance of preserving cultural heritage.
